claim: How to run: `agent.run()` is an async coroutine, so you wrap it in an async function and call `asyncio.run(main())`. This is the canonical pattern in both the official quickstart docs and the README. Minimal official quickstart example: `from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse; import asyncio; async def main(): agent = Agent(task="Find the number 1 post on Show HN", llm=ChatBrowserUse()); await agent.run(); asyncio.run(main())` (docs also use `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv()` for API keys).

import asyncio
from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse

async def main():
    agent = Agent(
        task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo",
        llm=ChatBrowserUse(model='openai/gpt-5.5'),
    )
    ...await agent.run()

asyncio.run(main())

claim: Max steps: `max_steps` is a parameter of `run()`, NOT of the Agent constructor. Exact signature in 0.13.3: `async def run(self, max_steps: int = 500, on_step_start=None, on_step_end=None) -> AgentHistoryList[AgentStructuredOutput]`. So limit steps with `await agent.run(max_steps=10)`. Note the default is 500 in 0.13.3 source; a web-search summary claimed default 100 (likely from an older version) — the 500 figure is verified directly from tagged source and wins. When max_steps is hit, the agent is forced to call the 'done' tool on the last step.

claim: Return value: `agent.run()` returns an `AgentHistoryList` (generic over AgentStructuredOutput; importable as `from browser_use import AgentHistoryList`, defined in browser_use/agent/views.py). Success vs failure: `history.is_done() -> bool` (agent issued its final 'done' action); `history.is_successful() -> bool | None` (True/False = the agent's own success judgment on the done step, None = never finished, e.g. ran out of max_steps); `history.final_result() -> str | None` (extracted_content of the last action, None if none); plus `history.has_errors() -> bool` and `history.errors() -> list[str | None]`. So the standard check is: result = await agent.run(); if result.is_successful(): ... (treat None as not-done/failure).
verifyReason: Verified directly against the cited source at tag 0.13.3 (raw.githubusercontent.com). browser_use/agent/views.py defines `class AgentHistoryList(BaseModel, Generic[AgentStructuredOutput])` with is_done(), is_successful() (returns None if not done, else last_result.success), final_result() (extracted_content or None), has_errors(), and errors() -> list[str | None] — all matching the claimed code verbatim. browser_use/__init__.py exports AgentHistoryList in its lazy-import map and __all__, so `from browser_use import AgentHistoryList` works. Agent.run in agent/service.py is annotated `-> AgentHistoryList[AgentStructuredOutput]`. Version check: 0.13.3 is the latest GitHub release (published 2026-07-01), so this describes the current API, not a stale/renamed one.
